dynamic capabilities, defined as sensing, seizing, or reconfiguration capabilities, are the capabilities that enable business enterprises to achieve and sustain superior performance.

dynamic capabilities are a set of skills and processes that create, deploy, or protect a firm’s intangible assets.

the nature and microfoundationsof dynamic capabilities, the skills, procedures, and organizational structures that undergird enterprise performance over the long term.

explicating the nature and micro-foundations of the capabilities which underlie superior enterprise performance in a world of rapidly changing technologies, globalized production, and intense competition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dynamic capability is a set of skills and processes through which enterprises adapt and reconfigure in response to changing demands and opportunities.
dynamic capabilities enable firms to sense and shape opportunities and threats, and reconfigure internal and external competences to address rapidly changing environments.
dynamic capabilities are those processes that use knowledge to integrate, reconfigure, gain and release resources—both tangible and intangible—to match and eventually create market change.

it is about the microfoundations of sustained superior enterprise performance in open, innovative economies.
